blocks.text: **Indradhanush** (Hindi for rainbow) is a **seven-pronged plan** launched in **August 2015** by the Finance Minister (**Arun Jaitley**) to **revamp the functioning of public sector banks (PSBs)**. Like a rainbow with seven colours, it has seven elements. It is also called **A2G** because the elements run alphabetically from A to G.

blocks.title: Mission
items: Revamp and improve the functioning of PSBs through **systemic changes** in state-run lenders.
A fresh look at **hiring** and appointments.
A comprehensive plan to **de-stress bloated lenders** (bad loans).
**Accountability** with incentives and higher rewards, including **stock options**.

blocks.title: Quick facts
blocks.text: Launched **August 2015**, by the **Finance Minister**, with **seven** elements; also known as **A2G** for public sector banks.

blocks.title: Rainbow = 7 = A to G
blocks.phrase: A Big Cat Does Extra Fast Gymnastics – the seven Indradhanush points in alphabetical order.
blocks.note: The seven points already come in A to G order, which is why the plan is also called A2G.

blocks.title: What each element means
rows: Executives from the **private sector** can be hired to run state-owned banks. The posts of **Chairman and Managing Director (CMD)** and **MD and CEO** are separated in PSBs, and private-sector candidates may also apply for MD and CEO.
Replaced the existing Appointments Board; an autonomous body of eminent professionals and officials.
The Government infuses capital into PSBs so they meet capital norms.
Relieve banks of **non-performing assets (bad loans)**; **asset reconstruction companies** are strengthened to deal with bad loans.
Government makes it easier for PSBs to **hire**, and looks at **Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs)** for PSB managements.
A new framework of **key performance indicators (KPIs)** for state-run lenders to boost efficiency, while assuring them **independence in purely commercial decisions**.
Process began with **Gyan Sangam**, a conclave of PSBs and financial institutions.

blocks.title: Which element does what?
blocks.phrase: Appoint people, Bureau picks, Capital pays, De-stress clears bad loans, Empower with ESOPs, Framework measures KPIs, Governance starts at Gyan Sangam.

blocks.text: Under the first capitalisation plan, **13 public sector banks** received capital of about **₹20,000 crore** in 2015-16, and the remaining part of the ₹25,000 crore provision for that year (about ₹5,000 crore) was allocated based on **efficiency criteria**. **State Bank of India** received the largest amount.

Total
blocks.text: The 13 allocations in the table add up to about **₹20,088 crore**. Several banks listed (Dena, Andhra, Corporation, Allahabad) no longer exist separately after the 2019-2020 mergers.

blocks.title: Top six in order of capital
blocks.phrase: Some Big Investors Own Big Property – SBI, BoI, IDBI, IOB, BoB, PNB (largest to smaller).

blocks.text: **Gyan Sangam** was a **conclave (bankers' retreat)** of PSBs and financial institutions held at the beginning of **2015 in Pune**. It was attended by all stakeholders, including the **Prime Minister, Finance Minister, Minister of State for Finance, RBI Governor and the CMDs** of all PSBs and financial institutions.

blocks.title: Outcomes
items: Each bank agreed to nominate a **senior officer as Chief Risk Officer (CRO)** of the bank.
It started the process of governance reforms, the seventh prong (G) of Indradhanush.

blocks.title: Gyan Sangam in one line
blocks.text: 'Gyan' = knowledge, 'Sangam' = meeting. A bankers' retreat in **Pune**, **early 2015**, that gave birth to governance reforms and **Chief Risk Officers**.

blocks.title: Funding roadmap announced in 2015
rows: **₹70,000 crore** into state-run banks **over four years**.
A further **₹1.1 lakh crore** to be raised by the banks themselves from the market.
To meet capital needs under **Basel III**, the global risk norms.

blocks.text: In **2017** the Government came out with **Indradhanush 2.0**, a comprehensive plan for **recapitalisation** of public sector lenders so that they stay solvent and fully comply with **Basel III** capital adequacy norms. It was linked to the completion of the **Asset Quality Review (AQR)** by the Reserve Bank, and aimed at cleaning up PSB balance sheets after the AQR and a **revised capitalisation programme**.

blocks.phrase: Seven-oh from the Government, one-ten from the market: 70,000 + 1,10,000 crore, about ₹1.8 lakh crore in all.
blocks.note: Indradhanush 1.0 = 2015; Indradhanush 2.0 = 2017, tied to Basel III and the RBI's AQR.

blocks.title: Do not confuse the years
blocks.text: Launch of Indradhanush = **2015**. Indradhanush 2.0 = **2017**. Gyan Sangam = early **2015**. The Banks Board Bureau began working on **1 April 2016**.

revision: Indradhanush: seven-pronged plan to revamp public sector banks, launched in August 2015 by the Finance Minister.
Also known as A2G: Appointments, Banks Board Bureau, Capitalisation, De-stressing, Empowerment, Framework of Accountability, Governance Reforms.
Appointments: private-sector executives can be hired; posts of CMD and MD and CEO are separated in PSBs.
Banks Board Bureau replaced the Appointments Board.
13 PSBs were capitalised in 2015-16 with about ₹20,000 crore; SBI received the highest (₹5,531 crore).
De-stressing: tackle NPAs and strengthen asset reconstruction companies.
Empowerment: easier hiring and Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs) for PSB managements.
Framework of Accountability: key performance indicators for state-run lenders.
Governance reforms began with Gyan Sangam, a bankers' conclave in Pune in early 2015.
Gyan Sangam led each bank to nominate a senior officer as Chief Risk Officer.
Roadmap: ₹70,000 crore from the Government over four years plus ₹1.1 lakh crore raised from markets (Basel III).
Indradhanush 2.0 (2017): recapitalisation to meet Basel III, linked to the RBI's Asset Quality Review.
